primary_sources_checked.title: LeetCode 322 — Coin Change
verified_claims: The input is an integer array of coin denominations and a target amount.
The required result is the fewest number of coins needed to make the amount, or -1 if no combination can make it.
Each denomination may be used an unlimited number of times.
The official constraints include positive denominations and amount in 0..10000.

primary_sources_checked.title: CoinChange deterministic Java validation
verified_claims: The candidate implementation compiles under javac 21.0.11.
It returns all three official example results and the documented oversized-denomination boundary result.
It matches an independent breadth-first-search shortest-path oracle on 961 generated cases covering every non-empty subset of {1,2,3,4,5} and amounts 0..30.

findings.finding: The candidate directly answers the minimum-coin objective and does not confuse LeetCode 322 with the combination-count objective of Coin Change II.

The state definition dp[x], dp[0] base case, unreachable sentinel, last-coin recurrence, and ascending-amount dependency order are mutually consistent and correctly exploit the official positive-denomination constraint.
Using amount+1 as the unreachable sentinel is valid under the official contract: any reachable amount uses at most amount coins because every denomination is a positive integer.

The stated O(amount * coins.length) time and O(amount) auxiliary-space bounds match the implementation, while null and negative-amount checks are explicitly identified as repository-local defensive behavior rather than LeetCode input requirements.
The reproducible validation is structurally independent of the DP implementation because it uses BFS as a shortest-path oracle across 961 generated cases, in addition to all official examples.

The follow-ups are problem-specific and test unbounded reuse, base-state semantics, unreachable-state handling, the 322-vs-518 distinction, and the BFS alternative; the project section avoids fabricated experience.
